issues.problem: The documented REST header is `apikey`, not `Authorization`.
issues.suggestion: Use `apikey: YOUR_API_KEY`, or the `apikey` query parameter. See [authentication documentation](https://docs.tomorrow.io/reference/api-authentication).

issues.problem: The free-tier limits are published, so `unknown` is incorrect.
issues.suggestion: Use `500 requests/day, 25 requests/hour, and 3 requests/second`. See [Tomorrow.io free-plan limits](https://support.tomorrow.io/hc/en-us/articles/20273728362644-Free-API-Plan-Rate-Limits).

issues.problem: Rate limits are published, contrary to the entry.
issues.suggestion: State the free-plan limits above and note that other plans have account-specific limits.

issues.problem: TomTom provides recurring free monthly requests per API, not merely unspecified trial credits.
issues.suggestion: Describe product-specific monthly allowances; Geocoding currently includes 20,000 free requests/month, while the legacy Search API includes 2,500. See [current TomTom pricing](https://docs.tomtom.com/pricing).

issues.problem: Current V4 documentation uses `Tracking-Api-Key`; the claimed Bearer alternative is unsupported and appears to conflate another authentication scheme.
issues.suggestion: Remove the Bearer statement and use only `Tracking-Api-Key: YOUR_API_KEY`. See [TrackingMore's version comparison](https://support.trackingmore.com/en/article/differences-among-3-versions-of-trackingmore-api-1ip0fmh/).

issues.problem: The current Free plan has zero tracking credits and does not include API keys; API access begins with paid/trial plans.
issues.suggestion: Set API free-tier availability to false and describe the time-limited free trial separately. See [current TrackingMore pricing](https://www.trackingmore.com/pricing).

issues.problem: The listed per-endpoint values do not match current V4 plan limits and appear mixed from older API versions.
issues.suggestion: Use the current plan-based limits: Basic 6 requests/second, Pro 10 requests/second, and Enterprise custom, while checking endpoint documentation for exceptions.

issues.problem: Production API access does not require a funded account. Tradier states that API access is free for every brokerage account holder, and its current setup guide issues production and sandbox tokens after account setup.
issues.suggestion: Say `API access is free for Tradier Brokerage account holders; trading, subscriptions, and regulatory fees may apply`. See [Tradier's API overview](https://production.tradier.com/businesses/fintechs) and [getting-started guide](https://docs.tradier.com/docs/getting-started).

issues.problem: Tradier publishes a complete rate-limit table.
issues.suggestion: Use: production Standard and Market Data 120 requests/minute; production Trading 60/minute; sandbox 60/minute for all three categories, per access token. See [rate-limit documentation](https://docs.tradier.com/docs/rate-limiting).

issues.problem: Apiary is no longer the current documentation home.
issues.suggestion: Use `https://docs.trakt.tv/`, the current official documentation site.

issues.problem: The claim that VIP users receive higher API request-rate limits is not present in the current limits and conflicts with the published common limits.
issues.suggestion: Remove `VIP higher`; retain 1,000 GET requests per 5 minutes for authenticated users and applications, plus 1 authenticated write per second. See [current Trakt rate limits](https://docs.trakt.tv/docs/rate-limiting).

issues.problem: The documented REST API root includes `/rest`; `/api/v2` is only a common prefix for several distinct products.
issues.suggestion: Use `https://transit.land/api/v2/rest`. See [Transitland REST documentation](https://www.transit.land/documentation/rest-api).

issues.problem: Transitland explicitly does not use the `Authorization` header.
issues.suggestion: Use the `apikey` query parameter or an `apikey` header. See [Transitland API configuration](https://www.transit.land/documentation).

issues.problem: The current free REST allowance is 10,000 queries/month, not 1,000 requests/day.
issues.suggestion: Use `REST API: 10,000 queries/month`; the same free plan also includes 1,000 routing queries/month and 100,000 vector tiles/month. See [current plans](https://www.transit.land/plans-pricing/).

issues.problem: The stated daily quota is incorrect and omits the monthly product-specific quotas.
issues.suggestion: Replace it with the current monthly allowances and identify the Professional REST allowance as 200,000 requests/month.

issues.problem: `Travis-API-Version: 3` selects the API version; it is not an authentication alternative.
issues.suggestion: State that authentication uses `Authorization: token YOUR_API_TOKEN`, while `Travis-API-Version: 3` is a separate required/recommended version header. See [Travis authentication documentation](https://developer.travis-ci.com/authentication).

issues.problem: Travis CI no longer advertises a generally available free hosted plan; current public plans start at $15/month, and its billing documentation says Free Trial Plans are unavailable.
issues.suggestion: Set the general hosted free tier to false or qualify that free OSS credits/partner queues may be available under special conditions. See [current Travis CI pricing](https://www.travis-ci.com/pricing/).

issues.problem: Paid access is not exclusively contact-sales partner pricing. The Content API has self-service pay-as-you-go billing, with volume pricing shown during checkout or under My Plans.
issues.suggestion: Use `Self-service pay-as-you-go per-call pricing; contact sales for usage above 500,000 calls/month or negotiated arrangements`. See the [current FAQ](https://tripadvisor-content-api.readme.io/reference/faq).

issues.problem: The request filters results to `restaurants`, but the snippet depicts the geographic entity Paris itself, so it is not consistent with the request.
issues.suggestion: Either change `category=restaurants` to `category=geos`, or replace the response with an actual Paris restaurant result. See the [Location Search interface](https://tripadvisor-content-api.readme.io/reference/searchforlocations).

issues.problem: Tumblr publishes default rate limits, so `not published` is incorrect.
issues.suggestion: Use `1,000 API calls/hour and 5,000 calls/day per consumer key`, while noting additional IP- and action-specific limits. See [Tumblr Developer Resources](https://help.tumblr.com/knowledge-base/developer-resources/).

issues.problem: The free API is not restricted to non-commercial use. Its CC BY-SA license permits use for any purpose when attribution and ShareAlike requirements are followed.
issues.suggestion: Use `Free under CC BY-SA with attribution and ShareAlike; paid plans provide alternative licensing, higher limits, and SLAs`. See [TVMaze API licensing](https://www.tvmaze.com/api).

issues.problem: Paid plans are currently published, so `null` is inaccurate.
issues.suggestion: Use `Startup $250/month, Small Business $500/month, Enterprise custom`, subject to current billing terms. See [TVMaze API plans](https://www.tvmaze.com/api/plans).

issues.problem: The free limit is published precisely rather than merely being commonly cited.
issues.suggestion: Use `at least 20 calls every 10 seconds per IP address`; clients should back off on HTTP 429. See [TVMaze rate limiting](https://www.tvmaze.com/api#rate-limiting).
